title: Platform Engineer Journey: Battle Deck (draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a short, tactical battle-deck for field reps engaging platform engineering orgs (SRE, infra, platform teams) evaluating inference runtimes.
- Focus is on the "why Redwood" migration story, common technical objections, demo script, and a 10-minute troubleshooting checklist for POCs.

Slide 1 — Title / Hook:
- Title: "Platform Engineer Journey: Predictable Inference at Scale"
- One-liner: "How to make LLM inference a measurable, predictable service in your infra stack."
- Talking tip: start with SLAs teams care about (p99 latency, tail latency, predictable cost per 1k tokens).

Slide 2 — Who we’re speaking to (persona map):
- Platform Engineer / SRE: cares about reliability, capacity planning, multitenancy, canarying.
- ML Platform: cares about model versioning, reproducibility, quantization and performance tradeoffs.
- Security/Compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
- Business owner/Feature PM: latency/cost impact on product metrics.

Slide 3 — Common evaluation triggers we see:
- Repeated cold starts and unpredictable token costs from naive batching.
- Increasing infra debt as teams hand-roll model serving and autoscaling.
- Regulatory requirement: need private deployments or VPC peering.
- Need for consistent dev -> prod parity across hosted/dedicated/private.

Slide 4 — Top 5 objections (and short rebuttals):
1) "We can run models ourselves, why a managed runtime?"
   - Rebuttal: MVP/POC is fine self-hosted; production-grade SLOs (p99 tail, predictable batching) cost more than infra. Redwood bundles runtime + ops + cost controls.
2) "Vendor lock-in concern"
   - Rebuttal: Same API across hosted/dedicated/private; model-version portability and exportable configs.
3) "Canarying models will slow us down"
   - Rebuttal: Built-in rollout primitives: traffic splitting, auto-fallback, model variant compatibility checks.
4) "Quantized models degrade quality"
   - Rebuttal: We provide model- and workload-specific quantization recommendations and quality monitoring with regression alerts.
5) "Price is opaque / per-token pricing is unpredictable"
   - Rebuttal: Show cost breakdowns (token, batching, KV cache savings) and Optimize suggestions. Provide pricing anchor from similar-scale customers.

Slide 5 — Rapid demo script (10 minutes):
- Setup (2m): show project, model catalog, pick a verified model.
- Warmup (2m): simulate traffic and show prefix/KV caching effects, reduced tail latency.
- Routing / fallback (2m): configure policy to route to cheaper variant when latency threshold or capacity trigger occurs.
- Observability (2m): open Console: token-level cost, p99/p95 charts, per-route traces.
- Canary rollback (2m): create a canary, push traffic, show automatic fallback when error spike is detected.

Slide 6 — Concrete metrics to show in POC (and how to measure):
- P99 latency pre/post Redwood (ms) — set synthetic steady-state and tail workloads.
- Cost per 1k tokens — include impact of batching and cache.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) under sustained QPS.
- Error rate under burst and degraded model variant fallback.

Slide 7 — Short technical architecture diagram (talking points only):
- Client -> Smart Router (policies: latency, cost, region) -> Serving runtime (batching + KV cache + quantized kernels) -> optional Private control plane (VPC).
- Emphasize interchangeable model variants and rollback hooks.

Slide 8 — POC success criteria (mutually agreed):
- Functional: <200ms median, <800ms p99 for typical prompts (adjust to customer SLAs).
- Economic: >=20% cost-per-token reduction vs current baseline or clear path via batching/quantization.
- Operational: one-page runbook for canaries + auto-fallback, documented SLOs and alerting.

Slide 9 — Quick objection playbook (bullet responses):
- "We need on-prem" -> Redwood Private + HSM/KMS + audit logs.
- "We will lose model fidelity" -> show eval harness and A/B model comparisons; rollback.
- "We can’t commit to monthly reserved" -> start hosted with usage cap, then Dedicated when throughput predictable.

Slide 10 — Competitive differentiator bullets (short):
- Unified API across deployment modes (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Production-first telemetry designed for token economics (not just model outputs).
- Built-in fallback and routing policies focused on keeping product availability high.

Slide 11 — Pricing anchor & contracting notes (field-friendly):
- Quick anchor examples: small PLG app: $X / month for hosted baseline; mid-scale (Dedicated) example with reserved capacity pricing and expected uplift for SLAs.
- Note to rep: escalate to pricing team (pricing@redwood) for custom reserved quotes.

Slide 12 — Demo checklists & troubleshooting (10-pt list):
- Confirm model selected is in catalog and has a verified performance profile.
- Ramp synthetic traffic to warm KV cache before measuring latency.
- Validate routing policy: simulate fallback condition.
- Check tokenization differences between customer tokenizer and chosen model.
- Confirm VPC peering and firewall rules for Private POC.
- Validate quantization profile and A/B eval comparison.
- Confirm logging level set to capture per-request token cost.
- Ensure canary window length matches typical traffic patterns.
- Validate autoscale thresholds on Dedicated pools.
- Capture baseline metrics for 48h before claiming savings.

Slide 13 — Next steps template (to share with prospect):
- 1) Proposed POC scope (2–4 weeks): target routes, traffic profile, success metrics.
- 2) Technical kickoff: exchange VPC details / service account + list of sample prompts.
- 3) 2-week checkpoint: show warmed results and initial cost delta.
- 4) Rollout plan: canary -> phased -> full cutover with rollback triggers.

Internal notes / TODOs (rough):
- Need customer-ready slide with pricing examples redacted for field (Samir to draft by EOD 1/16).
- Ask SRE for latest Dedicated autoscale endorsement copy (Lena).
- Add one page case study (short) from finance customer that saved 27% tokens costs via prefix caching. (Markus to pull metrics).
- Validate demo scripts against internal sandbox (PR #82 linked above).

Open questions for product:
- Can we expose a simple toggle that simulates "fallback-to-cheaper-variant" in hosted demo projects?
- Any upcoming telemetry fields related to per-user token attribution (required for finance customer's chargeback)?

Notes to self / field tips:
- Keep demo crisp: platform teams tune into the reliability story; show rollback and audit logs early.
- Avoid deep model internals unless asked; platform engineers want deploy/run/observe play.
- If they care about cost math, bring a quick spreadsheet comparing pre/post batching and cache.

Appendix (useful quick links):
- Internal POC runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/GT/pages/12345-platform-engineer-playbook

-- End draft --

(Format note: this doc is intentionally lean — primary deliverable is a 8–12 slide deck + one-pager POC scope. Use this as the script for recordings and quick live walk-throughs.)
